analysis_steps.goal: Homogenize PSFs, resample images, and measure aperture photometry and optical [O III] line map

method.value: Construct effective PSFs using photutils, create convolution kernels with PyPHER to match F444W (or ALMA clean beam), resample with reproject, perform fixed-aperture photometry with local sky annulus subtraction, and derive optical [O III] flux map from F356W-F444W excess.

evidence.quote: Then, we homogenized the PSFs of the NIRCam images using kernels created by PyPHER (cite: Boucaud.A:2016a).
Finally, the image pixels were resampled using reproject to match the F444W image pixels.
Photometry was performed with fixed apertures on the PSF-homogenized images and aperture correction was not applied.

We chose a circular aperture of 1.8\ensuremath{''} in diameter to measure the total photometry of B14-65666, which sufficiently recover all the fluxes according to curve-of-growth plots of the flux density.
The local sky background computed in an annulus from 0.95\ensuremath{''} to 1.95\ensuremath{''} were subtracted before the photometry measurements.

analysis_steps.goal: Perform UV-to-FIR SED fitting for total system and resolved components

method.value: Fit NIRCam photometry with and without ALMA Band 6, 7, 8 dust continuum and [O III] 88 um line fluxes using Bagpipes with BPASS v2.3 stellar models, CLOUDY nebular emission, and CIGALE Draine et al. (2014) dust emission models.

evidence.quote: We performed SED fitting to the NIRCam photometry using Bayesian Analysis of Galaxies for Physical Inference and Parameter EStimation (cite: Carnall.A:2018a).
We tested SED fitting with and without ALMA fluxes to see changes in obtained best-fit parameters.

Instead of the originally adopted ones, we used the updated version (cite: Draine.B:2014a) implemented in the CIGALE SED fitting code (cite: Boquien.M:2019a), which allows up to \ensuremath{\mathcal{U}_\mathrm{min}}= 50.
The redshift is fixed at z = 7.1520 in the fitting.

key_parameters.value: n_H = 100 cm^-3 (fixed in Bagpipes CLOUDY models)

evidence.quote: The hydrogen density in the CLOUDY models is fixed to be n_\text{H} = 100 \mathrm{cm^{-3}} in Bagpipes.

key_parameters.value: Old stellar component: constant SF from 600 to 100 Myr ago with Z_star = 0.5 Z_sun

evidence.quote: To constrain the mass of the old stellar components, we added another constant star formation lasting for 500 Myr, from 600 Myr ago to 100 Myr ago with respect to z = 7.15, which does not strongly contribute to UV continuum and emission-line fluxes.

The stellar metallicity of the old components is fixed to \ensuremath{Z_\text{star}}= 0.5 Z_\text{\(\odot\)} (cite: Asplund.M:2021a) to reduce the number of free parameters, but we checked that results do not vary significantly with the assumed Z_\text{star} value.

key_parameters.value: Dust parameters fixed: alpha_U = 2, U_max = 10^7, q_PAH = 2.5%

evidence.quote: The model parameters other than \mathcal{U}_\mathrm{min} and \gamma were fixed: the power-law index of the stellar intensity \alpha_\mathcal{U} = 2, the maximum stellar intensity \mathcal{U}_\text{max} = 10^7, and the PAH mass fraction q_\text{PAH} = 2.5%.
The dust attenuation curve follows the (cite: Calzetti:2000) law.

assumptions.value: Kroupa (2001) IMF from 0.1 to 300 M_sun and BPASS Delta log(alpha/Fe) = +0.6

evidence.quote: We used the case of \varDelta \log(\alpha/\text{Fe}) = +0.6, where the oxygen abundance is almost the solar value 12 + \log\ensuremath{\text{O}/\text{H}}= 8.69 (cite: Asplund.M:2021a) at Z = 0.02 (cite: Byrne.C:2022a).
The adopted initial mass function (IMF) is a (cite: Kroupa:2001) IMF in the mass range from 0.1 to 300 \mathrm{M_\ensuremath{\odot}}.

assumptions.value: Gas-phase metallicity identical to stellar metallicity

evidence.quote: The gas-phase metallicity is assumed to be identical to the stellar metallicity.

fitting.value: Nested sampling in Bagpipes with uniform priors: t_SF in [1.0, 300.0] Myr, log M* in [1.0, 15.0], A_V in [0.0, 2.0] mag, log U in [-4.0, -0.5], Z* in [0.01, 2.00] Z_sun, log M_old in [1.0, 15.0], U_min in [0.1, 50.0], gamma in [0.001, 1.0]; best-fit from 50th percentile and 1-sigma from 16th/84th percentiles

evidence.quote: The best-fit parameters are computed as the median of the posterior distributions. The 1\sigma fitting uncertainties are evaluated from the 16 and 84 percentiles of the posterior distributions.
Bagpipes receives these ranges as limits of the uniform prior distributions and performs the nested sampling to generate the posterior distribution of the parameters.

validation.value: Tested constant, delayed-tau, exponential, and no-old-component SFHs in Appendix and confirmed results are insensitive to SFH choice

evidence.quote: We also tested different star-formation histories, but the fitting results were insensitive to different star-formation histories

method.value: Compute monochromatic UV luminosity L_UV at 1600 A and UV spectral slope beta_UV via linear fitting to 500 posterior SED models (from NIRCam-only fits) in Calzetti et al. (1994) windows, combine with ALMA L_IR from Hashimoto et al. (2019), and compare against canonical Meurer and SMC relations.

evidence.quote: We computed the monochromatic rest-frame UV luminosity L_\text{UV} and \beta_\text{UV} from the best-fit SED models derived without the ALMA data.

The UV luminosity was computed from the UV continuum as L_\text{UV} = \lambda L_{\lambda} at \lambda = 1600 Å. The UV slope was obtained by linear fitting to the UV continuum within the wavelength windows proposed by (cite: Calzetti.D:1994a).

The IR luminosity L_\text{IR} was taken from (cite: Hashimoto.T:2019a), who estimated it by the modified blackbody fitting under the assumption of the dust temperature of T_\text{d} = 48 K and the dust emissivity of \beta_\text{d} = 2.0.
For simplicity we use \ensuremath{\beta_\text{UV,0}}= -2.62 (cite: Reddy.N:2018a) as a fiducial value at high redshift.

assumptions.value: Modified blackbody T_d = 48 K and beta_d = 2.0 for L_IR

evidence.quote: The IR luminosity L_\text{IR} was taken from (cite: Hashimoto.T:2019a), who estimated it by the modified blackbody fitting under the assumption of the dust temperature of T_\text{d} = 48 K and the dust emissivity of \beta_\text{d} = 2.0.

fitting.value: Linear fitting to the UV continuum in Calzetti et al. (1994) windows across 500 posterior SED models

evidence.quote: The UV slope was obtained by linear fitting to the UV continuum within the wavelength windows proposed by (cite: Calzetti.D:1994a).
we measured values from the 500 SED models derived from the parameter posterior distributions and estimated uncertainties from the measurement distribution.

validation.value: Checked intrinsic UV slope beta_UV,0 of best-fit SED curves before dust reddening (-2.6 to -2.55)

evidence.quote: We checked \beta_\text{UV,0} of our best-fit intrinsic SED curves before dust reddening and found that it ranges from \ensuremath{\beta_\text{UV,0}}= -2.6 to -2.55, which is bluer than -2.23 used in (cite: Meurer.G:1999a).

analysis_steps.goal: Construct optical-to-FIR [O III] line ratio map and model gas-phase metallicity

method.value: Correct F356W and F444W images for dust attenuation using best-fit A_V, convolve optical [O III] map to ALMA 0.38'' beam, divide by ALMA [O III] 88 um moment-0 map, and compare ratios with CLOUDY v17.02 photoionization models as a function of Z_gas, U, and n_e (computed with PyNeb).

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: We created a line-ratio map by taking a ratio of the optical [O iii]\lambda\lambda4960,5008 emission-line map to the FIR [O iii] 88 \mathrm{\mu m} image.

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: The created attenuation-corrected optical line map was convolved to match the angular resolution of the ALMA synthesized beam (0.38\ensuremath{''}).

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: To be more quantitative, we used CLOUDY to explore nebular parameters that reproduce the obtained [O iii] line ratios.

key_parameters.value: Aperture dust attenuation corrections: E (A_V = 1.2 mag), W (0.34 mag), E-core (0.72 mag)

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: We corrected flux densities within the apertures E (A_\text{V} = 1.2 mag), W (0.34 mag), and E-core (0.72 mag) so that the flux density recovered in each aperture agreed with the best-fit A_\text{V} value obtained in the SED fitting.

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: The created attenuation-corrected optical line map was convolved to match the angular resolution of the ALMA synthesized beam (0.38\ensuremath{''}).

key_parameters.value: CLOUDY stopping criterion: electron fraction = 10^-2; SFH = 10-Myr constant star formation

evidence.quote: The star-formation history is set to be a 10-Myr constant star formation.
The calculations stop at the edge of the H ii region where the electron fraction is 10^{-2}.

assumptions.value: Plane-parallel geometry under constant pressure; electron density n_e ~ 200-400 cm^-3; T_e = 1.2x10^4 K for PyNeb n_e calculation

evidence.quote: We assumed a plane-parallel geometry under the constant pressure and elemental and dust-grain abundances in the H ii regions that are stored in CLOUDY.

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity

findings_qualitative.value: B14-65666 is confirmed to be a major merger in a starburst phase with two spatially separated rest-frame optical components (E and W), ruling out a scenario of star-forming clumps within a single rotating disk.

evidence.loc: Morphology, Colors, and Optical [O iii] Line Map
evidence.quote: The two galaxies are apparently separated in the rest-frame optical wavelengths, ruling out a scenario that the two bright components are star-forming regions in a rotating stellar disk.

findings_qualitative.value: Galaxy E has an unresolved compact core surrounded by diffuse extended emission (likely tidal tails) that is bright in optical continuum/lines and ALMA [O III] 88 um, while galaxy W is elongated and clumpy.

evidence.quote: The high angular resolution of NIRCam reveals the complex morphology of two galaxy components: galaxy E has a compact core (E-core), surrounded by diffuse, extended, rest-frame optical emission, which is likely to be tidal tails; and galaxy W has a clumpy and elongated morphology with a blue UV slope (\ensuremath{\beta_\text{UV}}=-2.2\pm0.1).
ALMA archival data show that the bluer galaxy W is brighter in dust continua than the redder galaxy E, while the tails are bright in [O iii]  88 \mathrm{\mu m}.

findings_qualitative.value: Despite having a bluer UV slope, galaxy W is brighter in ALMA dust continuum at 88 and 158 um than the redder galaxy E, which can be explained by a higher dust temperature in galaxy E and/or lower dust temperature or patchy dust geometry in galaxy W.

evidence.quote: The galaxy E is a dusty (A_\text{V}=1.2\pm0.1 mag) starburst with a possible high dust temperature (\ge63\mbox{--}68 K). The galaxy W would have a low dust temperature (\le27\mbox{--}33 K) or patchy stellar-and-dust geometry, as suggested from the infrared excess (IRX) and \beta_\text{UV} diagram.

findings_qualitative.value: The E-core exhibits a higher optical-to-FIR [O III] line ratio and lower gas-phase metallicity than galaxy W, consistent with less-enriched gas inflows triggered by the major merger.

evidence.quote: The high optical-to-FIR [O iii] line ratio of the E-core shows its lower gas-phase metallicity (\simeq0.2\mbox{--}0.4 Z_\text{\(\odot\)}) than the galaxy W. These results agree with a scenario where major mergers disturb morphology and induce nuclear dusty starbursts triggered by less-enriched inflows.

claims.hypothesis: B14-65666 is a major merger system undergoing a merger-induced starburst rather than star-forming clumps in a rotating disk.
claims.experiment: Analyze rest-frame UV/optical morphology in six JWST NIRCam bands and perform UV-to-FIR SED fitting with Bagpipes to measure stellar masses and star-formation rates of the resolved components.
claims.result: Galaxies E and W are spatially separated in rest-frame optical, exhibit tidal tail features, have a stellar mass ratio of 3:1 to 2:1, and have a total instant SFR of ~230 M_sun/yr (~1 dex above the z~7 main sequence).
claims.finding: B14-65666 is confirmed as a major merger in terms of stellar mass ratio that is experiencing enhanced nuclear dusty starbursts.

evidence.quote: The UV/optical and sub-mm SED fitting confirms that B14-65666 is a major merger in a starburst phase as derived from the stellar mass ratio (3:1 to 2:1) and the star-formation rate, \simeq1 dex higher than the star-formation main sequence at the same redshift.

evidence.loc: Morphology, Colors, and Optical [O iii] Line Map
evidence.quote: The two galaxies are apparently separated in the rest-frame optical wavelengths, ruling out a scenario that the two bright components are star-forming regions in a rotating stellar disk.

claims.hypothesis: The counter-intuitive observation that the UV-bluer galaxy W is brighter in FIR dust continuum than the UV-redder galaxy E is caused by differences in dust temperature, attenuation curves, or dust-star geometry between the two components.
claims.experiment: Perform combined NIRCam+ALMA SED fitting with Draine et al. (2014) dust models and compare the resolved components on the IRX-beta_UV diagram.
claims.result: Total system follows the beta_UV,0-modified Meurer relation, but galaxy E lies below it (explained by T_d >= 63-68 K, steeper SMC-like attenuation, or tail contamination) and galaxy W lies above it (explained by T_d <= 27-33 K or patchy dust geometry).
claims.finding: Galaxies E and W have distinct dust properties (dust temperatures and/or patchy geometry) despite similar total IRX.

evidence.quote: The galaxy E is a dusty (A_\text{V}=1.2\pm0.1 mag) starburst with a possible high dust temperature (\ge63\mbox{--}68 K). The galaxy W would have a low dust temperature (\le27\mbox{--}33 K) or patchy stellar-and-dust geometry, as suggested from the infrared excess (IRX) and \beta_\text{UV} diagram.

The galaxies E and W are, however, not consistent with the \beta_\text{UV,0}-modified Meurer relation. The galaxies E and W exhibit lower and higher IRX than the relation at their \beta_\text{UV}, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: Major merger interaction induces inflows of less-enriched gas into the galaxy center, diluting central gas-phase metallicity and triggering a compact nuclear starburst.
claims.experiment: Construct a spatially resolved optical-to-FIR [O III] (4960,5008 A / 88 um) line ratio map from dust-corrected NIRCam and ALMA Band 8 images and compare with CLOUDY photoionization models and Bagpipes SED fits.
claims.result: The E-core has r_e < 85 pc, Sigma_SFR,0 >= 4x10^3 M_sun/yr/kpc^2, and an optical-to-FIR [O III] ratio of 9.2 (corresponding to Z_gas ~ 0.2-0.4 Z_sun), higher than the W-core ratio of 5.6 (Z_gas > 0.4 Z_sun).
claims.finding: The compact starburst at the E-core has lower gas-phase metallicity than galaxy W, supporting merger-driven inflow of less-enriched gas.

evidence.quote: The high optical-to-FIR [O iii] line ratio of the E-core shows its lower gas-phase metallicity (\simeq0.2\mbox{--}0.4 Z_\text{\(\odot\)}) than the galaxy W. These results agree with a scenario where major mergers disturb morphology and induce nuclear dusty starbursts triggered by less-enriched inflows.

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity
evidence.quote: Using the line ratios at the peak positions of the E-core and W-core, the E-core exhibits a lower gas-phase metallicity of Z\sim 0.2\mbox{--}0.4 Z_\text{\(\odot\)} than the W-core (> 0.4 Z_\text{\(\odot\)}).

evidence.loc: JWST and ALMA Observations and Data Reductions

evidence.loc: NIRCam and ALMA imaging: Stellar versus dust distribution
evidence.quote: The combination of the new NIRCam images with archival high angular-resolution (< 0.4\ensuremath{''}) ALMA data provides us with an unique opportunity to investigate the detailed stellar, ionized, and dust structure in an interacting system at z > 7.

why_this_method.value: Updated Draine et al. (2014) dust models in CIGALE allow U_min up to 50 needed for warm high-z dust; BPASS v2.3 binary models with alpha-enhancement reproduce strong high-z [O III] lines and hard UV slopes; optical-to-FIR [O III] ratio probes ionized gas temperature, density, and metallicity.

evidence.quote: Instead of the originally adopted ones, we used the updated version (cite: Draine.B:2014a) implemented in the CIGALE SED fitting code (cite: Boquien.M:2019a), which allows up to \ensuremath{\mathcal{U}_\mathrm{min}}= 50.
This enhancement of \alpha elements is also key to reproducing [O iii] emission line strengths and hard UV spectral slopes at high redshift (cite: Shapley.A:2019a; Sugahara.Y:2022a).

evidence.loc: [O iii] Line Ratio: Insights into Gas-phase Metallicity

In particular, the galaxy E requires so high \mathcal{U}_\mathrm{min} and \gamma that their probability distribution functions reach the maximum values of their permitted parameter ranges.

limitations_admitted.value: Properties of the diffuse tails are poorly constrained due to non-detections in F115W/F150W/F200W and dust continuum, degeneracies between old stars, dust, and emission lines, and angular resolution differences between NIRCam and ALMA; alternative origins like ionized outflows or offset old stars are not rejected.

evidence.quote: Although we have revealed many properties of the cores of the galaxies, less properties are constrained for the tails. This is mainly because it is difficult to solve the degeneracy in physics that can explain their red SED, dust non-detections, and detection of [O iii] 88 \mathrm{\mu m} emission, with different angular resolutions of the NIRCam and ALMA.

We expected that the extended diffuse emission originates from the tidal tails produced by the major merger, but we did not reject other possibilities like ionized gas outflows (cite: Yuma.S:2019a) and offset old stellar populations (cite: Colina.L:2023a).

referee_caveats_inferred: Mismatch between 2D Gaussian fitting for ALMA photometry (inherited from Hashimoto et al. 2019) and fixed rectangular/circular aperture photometry for JWST NIRCam in the joint UV-to-FIR SED fitting.

Optical [O III] 4960,5008 line fluxes are derived purely from broad-band F356W - F444W color excess rather than spectroscopy, making the optical-to-FIR [O III] line ratio sensitive to assumed continuum slope, Hbeta/Hgamma/Hdelta subtraction, and spatially uniform aperture A_V corrections.
